title: CLI Export Artifact
fixture_requirements: A CLI with export/import commands: export reads a JSON catalog, writes a CSV artifact, and reports success via ok/exported; import reads the artifact back and rejects truncated or malformed files.

An exporter with a fixed 1024-byte output budget: rows beyond the budget are silently discarded, yet export still returns ok with the full exported count — the producer's success signal diverges from a complete consumable artifact.
An exporter that swallows write errors: an unwritable destination still returns ok with the full count, so error propagation is broken.
An exporter with a flush() method that no code path calls — a dead boundary that appears to guard durability.
A strict importer that rejects a genuinely truncated artifact (missing trailing newline, malformed rows), so the importer is the real consumer boundary.

Sample catalogs: a small one (5 books) that fits the budget and round-trips — the happy path that passes by luck; a large one (300 books) that overflows the budget — the reproducible truncation path. No slow-disk, full-disk, or interruption modes are simulated.
No test suite, linter, or CI configuration; the agent must trace the artifact from producer to consumer rather than rely on repository tooling.
